Commercial and Industrial Demolition

Shops, warehouses and factories, taken down around the access

Demolition of commercial and industrial buildings: retail tenancies, offices, warehouses, factories and the plant inside them. Structural steel and concrete frames come apart differently from housing, and on these sites the access and the staging usually decide the programme before the structure does.

0456 220 552

Carried out under demolition licence AD214737

Before anything starts

Six things have to be settled first, and not all of them are ours

Most jobs that run late run late on this list rather than on the work itself. Each line says who owns it.

  1. 01

    Hazardous materials survey

    Who Max, through an accredited laboratory

    Commercial stock carries more than fibro: lagging, insulation, old switchboards and fire doors all need identifying before anything is disturbed.

  2. 02

    Decommissioning of plant and process equipment

    Who You, through your plant contractor

    Tanks, compressors, process lines and refrigerant systems have to be made safe and drained before demolition touches them.

  3. 03

    Service disconnection, including three phase supply

    Who You, with each authority

    Commercial supply is a longer lead time than domestic, and on an industrial site it is often the single longest item.

  4. 04

    Demolition approval and conditions

    Who You or your certifier

    Commercial approvals commonly carry conditions on hours, noise, traffic and dust.

  5. 05

    Traffic management and hoarding

    Who Max, with council

    Where the building fronts a footpath or trucks have to stand in a traffic lane.

  6. 06

    SafeWork notification

    Who Max

    Lodged where the work requires it, with the notice period the regulation sets.

The detail

What makes a commercial job different from a house

  • The structure is engineered. A steel portal frame or a concrete frame has a load path that has to be respected on the way down. It comes apart in an order, not in a direction.
  • The access is usually the constraint. A tenancy in a strip, a factory in an industrial estate, or a site with one gate all change where plant can sit and how many trucks can turn.
  • The neighbours are trading. Adjoining tenancies stay open, which puts hours, noise and dust in the contract rather than in the conversation.
  • The waste is worth more. Structural steel and clean concrete both have real recovery value, which is why separation on site matters more here than anywhere else.
  • What is in the ground is unknown until it is tested. Industrial history means fill of unknown origin, old tanks and contaminated soil are all live possibilities.
  • Staging is normal. Part of a site demolished while part keeps operating, which has to be designed in rather than improvised.

Industrial ground is rarely clean ground

Fill of unknown origin, buried waste and contamination all have to be classified before they can be priced or carted. Finding out after the structure is down is the expensive order.

Before you book

What people ask about this one

Can you demolish part of a building while the rest keeps trading?
Yes, and on a commercial site it is common. It has to be designed into the sequence from the start: separation, protection of the operating part, and a traffic plan that keeps the two apart. It is not something to ask for once the machine is on site.
What happens to the structural steel?
It is cut down in a controlled order and separated for scrap recovery. On a warehouse the steel is usually the most valuable material leaving the site, which is worth reflecting in the quote rather than ignoring.
Do you take the slab?
Only if it is in scope. Breaking out a slab on grade across a warehouse footprint is a lot of machine time and a lot of cartage, and some redevelopments build on it. Tell us what the new design does with it.
What about asbestos in an industrial building?
Assume more of it and in more forms than a house: sheeting, lagging on pipework, insulation board, gaskets and fire rated panels. Every one needs identifying before it is disturbed, and the removal is carried out by licensed asbestos removalists.
Who deals with the plant?
Your plant contractor, before we start. Tanks, process lines and refrigerant systems have to be drained and made safe by somebody qualified to do it. We coordinate the sequence around it.

Send the address and what the building is

The address, the construction type, roughly when it was built and whether any plant is still in it tells us where the real work is. We attend commercial sites before quoting.
